title: Candy
prompt: There are `n` children standing in a line, each assigned a rating value given in the array `ratings`. You must give at least one candy to each child, and any child with a higher rating than an immediate neighbor must receive more candies than that neighbor. Return the minimum number of candies needed to satisfy these requirements.

examples.explanation: Give candies [2,1,2]: the child with rating 1 gets 2 candies, the child with rating 0 gets 1, and the child with rating 2 gets 2. Total is 5.
Give candies [1,2,1]. The third child gets 1 candy since equal ratings don't require more candies than a neighbor. Total is 4.

hints: Each child's requirement depends on both neighbors at once, which is hard to satisfy in a single left-to-right pass alone.

Split the constraint into two separate one-directional passes: one that only enforces 'higher than left neighbor implies more candies', and one that only enforces 'higher than right neighbor implies more candies'.

Do a left-to-right pass giving each child +1 more candy than their left neighbor if their rating is higher. Then do a right-to-left pass similarly for the right neighbor, taking the max of the two passes' results for each child, since each child must satisfy both constraints simultaneously.

solution.approach: Start every child with 1 candy. In a left-to-right pass, whenever a child's rating is higher than the child to their left, set their candy count to at least one more than their left neighbor's, which enforces the left-neighbor constraint. In a right-to-left pass, whenever a child's rating is higher than the child to their right, update their candy count to be at least one more than their right neighbor's count using max (since the left pass might have already given them more than needed) -- this enforces the right-neighbor constraint without breaking the left one. Summing the final per-child candy counts gives the minimum total, because each child ends up with exactly enough to satisfy whichever of their two neighbor constraints demands more.
